source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Record the date and time of the inspection.
3. Identify the inspector's name or identification number.
4. Enter the vehicle identification number (VIN) of the tested vehicle.
5. Record the make, model, year, and odometer reading of the vehicle.
6. Note the specific brake test performed (e.g., hydraulic pressure test, ABS diagnostic, deceleration test).
7. Document the brake system components tested: brakes (front, rear), rotors, calipers, drums, brake pads, brake lines, master cylinder, and fluid reservoir.
8. Detail any observed issues: leaks, wear, damage, or malfunctions.
9. Record any measurement values obtained during the test(s) (e.g., brake line pressure readings, deceleration rates).
10. Highlight failed tests and criteria:
     - List which specific brake standards or thresholds were not met (e.g., minimum brake fluid level, acceptable deceleration time).
